1. **Assess & design target**: Inventory schema, extensions, roles, and 2 TB data volume; provision the managed PostgreSQL instance sized for current + projected load; match version/extensions; configure networking, security groups, and encryption to match compliance requirements.
2. **Set up replication tooling**: Install/configure logical replication (e.g., native `pg_logical`/`publication-subscription`) or a managed CDC tool (AWS DMS, Google DMS, etc.) between on-prem source and cloud target so change data capture can run continuously ahead of cutover.
3. **Full baseline backup**: Take a full verified backup (pg_basebackup or pg_dump/pg_restore-tested) of the current production database before any replication setup touches production, and confirm it is restorable.
4. **Dry run / rehearsal on non-production data**: Clone production schema plus a representative/anonymized data subset (or a full staging copy) to the target service, run the entire migration + cutover script end-to-end, time each phase, and validate the two-hour window is sufficient.
5. **Stakeholder communication (advance notice)**: Notify the ~4,000 DAUs and internal stakeholders at least one week ahead of the scheduled Sunday maintenance window, with reminders at 48h and 2h before, stating expected downtime and rollback contingency.
6. **Pre-cutover full backup**: Immediately before the maintenance window, take a fresh full backup/snapshot of production (superseding step 3's backup) so there is a guaranteed restore point capturing the latest state prior to any write-blocking or schema changes.
7. **Begin initial bulk load + ongoing replication**: Start the bulk copy of the 2 TB dataset to the cloud target well before the window (days in advance) via the CDC/replication tool, letting it catch up continuously so only a small delta remains at cutover time.
8. **Enter maintenance window — freeze writes**: Put the application into read-only/maintenance mode, stop writer connections to on-prem Postgres, and let replication drain the final delta to the cloud target.
9. **Cutover**: Verify replication lag is zero, promote the cloud instance as primary, repoint application connection strings/DNS to the managed service, and re-enable write traffic.
10. **Data integrity verification**: Compare row counts, checksums (e.g., `pg_checksums`, table-level `md5`/hash aggregates), and key sequence/max-ID values between source and target for all critical tables; run smoke tests against the application before fully reopening traffic.
11. **Rollback procedure (trigger if verification fails or critical errors occur within window)**: Repoint application back to the on-prem server, re-enable writes there using the step 6 backup (plus any replayed WAL/CDC delta captured during the attempt) to restore consistency, notify stakeholders of the rollback, and preserve cloud-side logs/data for root-cause analysis before retrying on a future date.
12. **Post-migration close-out communication**: Notify stakeholders of success (or rollback) and completion time, monitor performance/error rates on the new managed service for the following 24–48 hours, and decommission or archive the on-prem instance only after a defined retention/observation period.
